blocks.md: This lesson follows **Choosing the Next Capability** in *Engineering Physical AI* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Engineering Physical AI, § Choosing the Next Capability
blocks.md: Pouring engineering effort into a faster proposer when an unmeasured floor or an unseated tab actually limits the cell leaves the operating restriction in place. In a deployed packaging cell, restricted transit speeds and human-supervised sign-offs call for different investments. Speeding up proposal generation improves throughput inside the current safety envelope, whereas qualifying a new contact or engagement sensor can retire the need for human sign-off altogether. Each advance requires two deliverables: a predeclared task metric and a physical test of the operating premise it changes.

questions.q: The section **Choosing the Next Capability** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: When two states that need different responses produce identical observations until the action deadline, no model on that channel can separate them, and the latest useful observation is set by braking distance over speed.

A premise no onboard sensor reports is not the envelope's monitored unknown, so it is bound to a standing restriction, an accountable owner, and a predeclared closure test, chosen among responses (probe, restrict, add sensing, accept by judgment) by the claim each can support.

Open register entries fall into classes by the evidence they lack (an unmeasured observable, an evaluation deficit, a theoretical deficit) or by a scope mismatch that no evidence inside the present architecture repairs, and the class, not the urgency, selects the next experiment, with each restriction priced against the campaign that would retire it.

A shield's per-command guarantee becomes a hazard-rate claim only conditionally, lambda_sys <= lambda_h(1 - c) + lambda_cc, and observed fleet rates already include the shield, so multiplying them by an interception factor double-counts.
